findings.description: GrokHeadlessAdapter.wire_effort constructs an uninitialized adapter with cls.__new__(cls), skipping __init__ (no config, logger, or circuit-breaker state), builds a synthetic CompletionRequest(messages=[]) and calls _resolve_reasoning_effort on that bare object. This is the value cheval records as effort_effective in the MODELINV audit envelope for xai routes. Any instance-attribute access inside _resolve_reasoning_effort, including a warning path that formats self.config or self.name, raises AttributeError at audit time. Because the value is derived by a side path rather than read back from the argv that _build_command actually emits, the audit field can silently diverge from the real --reasoning-effort token. The method also accepts an effort argument that its own docstring says is ignored, and it assumes CompletionRequest is a runtime import in this module. The new test module adds no test for wire_effort; _effort_on_wire coverage stops at anthropic and openai.
findings.failure_mode: On a grok-headless invocation, computing effort_effective either throws (aborting or failing the invoke depending on where _effort_on_wire is called relative to dispatch) or records a value that does not match the subprocess argv. The audit trail for model invocations becomes unreliable on exactly the provider whose effort handling differs from the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the reasoning-effort resolver a pure staticmethod that takes only the extra mapping and call it from both _build_command and wire_effort, or have wire_effort invoke the real argv builder and read the --reasoning-effort value back. Remove the ignored effort parameter or document it explicitly. Wrap the call site in cheval so an exception degrades to effort_effective=None with a WARN rather than failing the invoke. Add a unit test for wire_effort and an xai case to test_effort_on_wire_follows_the_adapter_mapping.

findings.description: The dry-run subprocess helper copies the full parent environment and removes only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK and CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN. Every other provider credential cheval can read (OpenAI, xAI, Google/Gemini, OpenRouter, and any future one) still reaches a child process that runs the complete cheval.py entrypoint. Safety depends solely on --dry-run never dispatching.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in dry-run gating, or a test edit that drops the --dry-run flag, makes the suite perform live, billed API calls with the developer's or CI runner's real credentials. Captured stdout/stderr then appears in assertion messages and CI logs, which may include provider error bodies.
findings.suggested_fix: Construct the child environment from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, PYTHONPATH, LANG/LC_*, TMPDIR) rather than a deny-list, and inject placeholder values for any variable cheval needs to resolve a provider in dry-run mode.

findings.description: The in-process invoke helper patches loa_cheval.audit.modelinv.redact_payload_strings to the identity function and assert_no_secret_shapes_remain to a no-op before capturing the MODELINV payload. All assertions on effort, effort_source and effort_effective therefore run against the pre-redaction payload. The new envelope fields are never shown to survive the redaction gate, and the secret-shape assertion that normally guards the audit sink is silenced for every test in this module.
findings.failure_mode: A redaction change that strips or rewrites the new fields, or a regression that lets a secret-shaped string into the envelope alongside them, passes this suite unnoticed. The tests give false assurance about what actually lands in the audit log.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep redaction and the secret-shape assertion active (they should be no-ops for these payloads) and stub only audit_emit. If the identity patch exists to dodge a specific redaction false positive, scope it to that single test and add an explicit assertion that the real redactor preserves effort_source and effort_effective.
